newsitem.title: BELARUS: SOCCER-SWEDEN ON GUARD AGAINST TRICKY BELARUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDEN ON GUARD AGAINST TRICKY BELARUS.

text.p: Belarus have nothing but pride left to play for the World Cup qualifying campaign but their solid display against Scotland in June has worried Sweden, who really need a win in Minsk on Wednesday to keep their hopes alive.

Swedish midfielder Jonas Thern said his Glasgow Rangers team mate, Scottish international Gordon Durie, had warned him to expect a poor surface and an awkward time before and after the game in Minsk. "He warned me not to underestimate the Belarussians," Thern said.
Swedish coach Tommy Svensson is predicting a tougher match than the home tie, when Sweden ran out 5-1 winners back in June 1996.
"We mustn't forget that Scotland had big problems dealing with Belarus," he told reporters.

The Scots, who lead the group, needed a Gary McAllister penalty to squeeze past the Belarussians 1-0 and coach Craig Brown predicted the improving ex-Soviet side would do his side a favour by taking points off challengers Austria and Sweden.
Helsingborg midfielder Andreas Jacobsen has withdrawn from the 19-strong Swedish squad with a knee injury, but the team looks set to be at virtually full strength.
Belarus squad spokesman Alexander Chernukha said his side, many of who play in the Russian league, were fit and eager for the fray.
"Of course, we have no chance of qualifying," he said. "But we realise the result of this game will decide the fate of several other teams."
Sweden lie third in the group, five points behind Scotland with two games in hand and one point behind Austria, who have played the same number of games.
